title: Why You Need a High Quality Headset To Fully Appreciate GTA 6
summary: GTA 6 is packed full of subtle audio details you may miss if you don't have a high quality headset like the award-winning Stealth™ Pro II.
body_markdown:
GTA 6 is out now, and wow, “detailed” doesn’t even begin to describe just how microscopically dense the game is with amazing content to discover ­— everything from stunning visuals, deep NPC interactions, an expansive map with hundreds of unique locations, and over 170 unique animals you can discover throughout Leonida, and that’s just scratching the surface of how much detail there truly is.


One area we know for sure that Rockstar jam-packed with fidelity is in the audio department. In a recent report by Eurogamer, Rockstar Vice President of Audio Alastair MacGregor explained the dynamic soundscape present in the game:


“…Convenience store refrigerators all have their own unique sounds. In a run-down store, the refrigerators and freezers are loud and sound like they are badly maintained. Their compressor units can be heard mechanically whirring away from years of neglect… In an up-market store, the refrigerators are quieter, adding a subtle hum to the environment."


It sounds (no pun intended) like the audio in GTA 6 is designed to immediately make the environments you move through emanate a sense of either low or high status without you even having to look at the screen. It’s the kind of attention to detail that truly engages your senses and deepens your immersion. MacGregor continues:


“…We love the contrast between the manicured luxury islands, with the sizzle of crickets and lawn sprinklers backed by birdsong, yacht halyards clanging in the distance, and yard work going on, versus urban areas with the sounds of people living on top of each other - snatches of every genre of music, distant voices, cars peeling out, construction, the omnipresent hum of elderly air conditioners struggling with the humidity."


That’s the kind of auditory contrast you’re never going to get if you play on mute or have a substandard audio solution that drowns out subtle sounds. You know how your TV can sometimes struggle to play dialogue loud enough to hear? Multiply that by the vast amount of minute sound effect details packed into this game, and it becomes simply tragic to think about everything you could be missing out on.


MacGregor says his team spent years iterating on reverb technology to make the player feel the impact of those myriad interacting and contrasting sounds, which sounds (pun intended) like time well spent to me. And, if I’m being honest, I’m willing to trust any guy named Alastair MacGregor when it comes to audio. He has a name of a guy who was born to be in a band.


If you’re stuck listening to GTA 6 through crappy TV speakers that crunch all sound subtlety into a cacophonous mess, though, you’re going to miss out Alastair & Co.’s painstakingly constructed dynamic audio soundscapes. That’s not cool!
